scope: Review of single-store deletion against the acceptance criteria. No store was created, deleted, or modified. No deletion or provisioning request was sent.
criteriaSource: docs/verification/multi-store-acceptance.md (85 sub-criteria; deletion behaviour also described in docs/multi-store.md)

deletionCriteria.MS-04a: Only that store's registration and grants are removed
deletionCriteria.MS-04c: PVC and PV cleanup is deterministic
deletionCriteria.MS-04g: Failed delete reports a reason and can retry
deletionCriteria.MS-04h: Other stores and the demo stay
deletionCriteria.MS-06g: Admission denies cross-namespace writes (PV delete limited to st-<16 hex> claims)
deletionCriteria.MS-08-11: Delete Store A from the dashboard
deletionCriteria.MS-08-12: Store A tools disappear from discovery
deletionCriteria.MS-08-13: Old tool name rejected and upstream not called
deletionCriteria.MS-08-14: Namespace, workloads, Secrets, Services, volumes, registry, and grants match the cleanup rules
deletionCriteria.MS-08-15: Store B stays Ready and its list_orders still runs
deletionCriteria.MS-08-16: Audit rows exist for create, chat, delete, and the denied stale call

implementation.api: apps/gateway/app/stores/api.py: POST /admin/stores/{id}/delete (session user; 202 deleting, 200 already deleted); GET /admin/stores/{id}/deletion
implementation.ownership: StoreService.get_owned (service.py:153): wrong owner returns not_found and audits admin:store_denied unauthorized
implementation.request: StoreService.request_delete (service.py:173): row -> deleting, phase unregister, attempt 0, deadline = now + timeout; revoke_store_grants (store_<id>__*) and delete_upstream before any cluster call; audits admin:delete_store success; repeat on a deleted row re-revokes grants and returns 200
implementation.teardown: StoreService._teardown (service.py:479): re-deregisters; cluster.delete_namespace; polls namespace_absent; release_store_volumes; only then state deleted
implementation.progressAccounting: _note_delete_incomplete (service.py:548): attempt counts failed API calls only, capped at max_attempts; a terminating namespace or bound volume is normal progress and reported delete_blocked only after the deadline; retries continue
implementation.clusterGuards: cluster.py: assert_store_namespace requires st-<store_id> and refuses protected namespaces; delete_namespace and namespace_absent require the urumi.dev/store-id label to match (OwnershipError otherwise, store marked failed without cleanup); release_store_volumes deletes only Released/Failed/Available PVs whose claimRef.namespace is that namespace; Bound/Pending keep the row deleting
implementation.admission: helm/urumi/templates/store-provisioner-admission.yaml limits provisioner writes to st-<16 hex> namespaces with matching labels and PV deletes to st-<16 hex> claim namespaces
implementation.routing: stores/routing.py: store tools are callable only when the caller owns a Ready store, so a deleting or deleted store's tools are denied before any upstream call

store-a-delete-preflight-blocked-2026102.whatItIs: A stopped attempt. No delete request was sent.
proves: Preflight state at revision 7 (two Ready stores, 7 PVs, StorageClass reclaim Delete) and a written review of delete semantics.
doesNotProve: Any deletion behaviour. It must not be cited as a deletion or as a safeguard blocking deletion; it stopped because a pre-delete test key was unavailable.

store-a-delete-20261025T085339Z.json.whatItIs: One live deletion of Store A (c4421147ea825bbc) through POST /admin/stores/c4421147ea825bbc/delete at 08:51Z on Helm revision 7 (image urumi-gateway:pvc-labels-20261025T080649Z).

Store A upstream and grant removed; Store B upstream and grant kept (MS-03j, MS-04a)

Audit rows admin:delete_store success and the denied stale call (part of MS-08-16)
doesNotProve: The dashboard delete button (API only) (MS-01d, MS-08-11)
Resume after a provisioner restart (MS-04f, MS-07f)
An induced failure and retry (MS-04g); the observed 'That store could not be deleted.' came from a counting defect during normal termination
Wrong-owner delete denial (MS-06f); only one user exists
Retain-policy volume sweep: reclaim was Delete, so release_store_volumes found nothing to delete
Admission denying an out-of-scope delete by the provisioner during teardown
The deployed delete-retry fix: the run used revision 7 code; the fix shipped in the revision 8 image and is in revision 10, but no deletion has run on it

automatedTests.isolation: All deletion tests use FakeCluster or a scripted HTTP opener against https://kubernetes.example. None constructs a real cluster client or reads a kubeconfig.
automatedTests.notRun: tests/test_postgres_permissions.py (includes test_store_grant_revoke_keeps_other_prefixes) needs a Docker PostgreSQL; not run in this pass.

coverage.dashboard: StorePanel.test.tsx 'confirms deletion of the named store and renders a failure reason'

testGaps: No test asserts the admin:delete_store audit row (fields or presence).
No audit row is written when a deletion completes (state deleted); no test covers that because the code does not do it.
No test deletes a store while a provisioning pass for it is in flight.
Resume is tested as a repeated reconcile on a held deletion, not as a worker restart that reloads deleting rows.
request_delete audits success when the request is accepted even if deregistration failed and will be retried; no test pins that behaviour.

verifiedByAutomatedTestsOnly: ownership and protected-namespace refusal during teardown
partial: MS-01d and MS-08-11 (API, not dashboard button)
MS-08-16 (no chat row in that run; delete completion is not separately audited)
MS-06g and MS-06i (admission denial shown for one ConfigMap create in default, not for a delete)
notVerifiedLive: Dashboard delete button on the cluster
Induced delete failure and recovery on the deployed fix (revision 8+)
Wrong-owner delete on the cluster (needs a second user)
Retain-policy volume sweep (cluster StorageClass is Delete)

nextSafeDemonstration.summary: One disposable store owned by the existing admin (cap is 3; the owner has 2 active stores), created and deleted through the dashboard on revision 10. Store B and Store C are never targeted.
nextSafeDemonstration.capacity: Per-store requests are about WordPress 256Mi, MariaDB 256Mi, MCP 64Mi plus an init Job. Node is about 3.07 GiB of 7.58 GiB; host available about 2.2 GiB. Stop if host available falls below 1500 MiB or the node exceeds 4.5 GiB.
steps: Preflight: release revision 10 deployed; Store B and C Ready; record uids of all Store B/C objects, all 7 PVs, upstream rows, grants, audit max id; memory gates.

Create store 'disposable-delete-demo' from the dashboard form; record the returned store id; confirm it is not 174c75b6c0ef57e5 or 5bc7dc01da3ccf38 and its namespace is st-<new id> with the matching store-id label; wait for Ready.
Optional, needs approval: create a member user and confirm its delete request for the new store returns not found and audits admin:store_denied.
Delete from the dashboard button, confirming the dialog names the new store; poll GET /admin/stores/<new id>/deletion.
Send the same delete again while Deleting (expect 202, no second attempt counted).

While the namespace is Terminating, restart only the provisioner (kubectl --context kind-urumi-k8s-test -n default rollout restart deploy/urumi-store-provisioner) and confirm the new pod resumes and the row reaches Deleted without delete_blocked.

Verify: namespace absent; no PV with claimRef.namespace st-<new id>; upstream row and store_<new id>__* grants gone; tools/list omits the store; a call to store_<new id>__list_orders is denied with no upstream; audit rows admin:create_store, admin:delete_store, and the denied call.
Verify Store B and C: same object uids, Ready, 0 restarts, same 7 PVs, upstreams and grants unchanged; one authorized list_orders on each if a new short-lived key is approved.
Write a new evidence file; do not modify earlier evidence.
guards: Every kubectl and helm command names --context or --kube-context kind-urumi-k8s-test.
Before each destructive request, compare the target store id against an allowlist containing only the new id.
No kubectl delete of namespaces, PVCs, or PVs by hand.
Abort and leave the store in place if the new id is ambiguous or any Store B/C uid changes.

mutations: none; read-only queries and non-destructive tests only
